औद्दालकीय: Auddālakīya nt.: Name of an आख्यान mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan (सावित्र्यौद्दालकीयं च) 1. 2. 126. Not found as an independent आख्यान in the Āraṇyakakaparvan; reference to 3. 132 ?
और्व: Aurva nt.: Name of an आख्यान mentioned while listing the contents of the Ādiparvan 1. 2. 87. Described as best (1. 2. 87); it occurs as a section (1. 169-172) of the Caitra-rathaparvan 1. 153-173.
औशनस: Auśanasa adj.: of a शास्त्र proclaimed by Uśanas; mentioned along with Bṛhaspati-mata 12. 122. 11. Uśanas and Bṛhaspati were to revive the शास्त्र proclaimed by the seven sages (Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha 12. 322. 26-27, 29; (its contents 12. 322. 30); 12. 322. 42-43 (उशना बृहस्पतिश् चैव यदोत्पन्नौ भविष्यतः । तदा प्रवक्ष्यतः शास्त्रम् युष्मन्मतिभिर् उद्धृतम्); it was learnt by king Vasuhoma, who had also learnt the शास्त्र (मत) of Bṛhaspati (बृहस्पतेर् मतं राजन्न् अधीतं सकलं त्वया । तथैवौशनसं शास्त्रं विज्ञातं ते नराधिप ॥ ), and there-fore king Māndhātṛ wanted to know from Vasuhoma how दण्ड came into existence for the maintenance of discipline among the subjects (प्रजाविनयरक्षार्थम्) 12. 122. 12-14. [See Bṛhaspatimata]

Auśanasa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ, also called Kapālamocana (3. 81. 118; 9. 38. 4, 8, 20). A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्यास् तीर्थवरम्) 9. 38. 16. B. Description: Best (उत्तम) 9. 38. 7; (अनु-त्तम) 9. 38. 16; excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थ-वर) 9. 38. 16, (तीर्थप्रवर) 9. 38. 7; famous (ख्यात) 9. 38. 16; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 81. 116; removing or destroying all sins (सर्वपाप-प्रमोचन) 3. 81. 118; (सर्वपापप्रश-मन) 9. 38. 16; inhabited by the Siddhas (सिद्धक्षेत्र) 9. 38. 16. C. Event: For-merly Kāvya (Uśanas) practised austerities at this तीर्थ (hence, perhaps, called Auśanasa); the whole नीति flashed before him, and there he pondered over the battle of the Daityas and the Dānavas (तत्रस्थश् चिन्तयाम् आस दैत्यदानवविग्रहम्) 9. 38. 6. D. Its name Kapālamocana explained by Vaiśaṃ-pāyana: Rāma, of the Raghu family, while in the Daṇḍakāraṇya, cut off the head of a demon with a razor-sharp arrow; the flying head, by chance, struck the flank (जङ्घा) of an ascetic named Mahodara and got stuck there; the ascetic could not get it out of the जङ्घा although he visited and bathed in many तीर्थस्; on the advice of some ascetics he went to the Auśanasatīrtha and bathed there; the head then came out of the जङ्घा and fell into the water; when the incident was reported to the ascetics they named Auśanasa as Kapālamocana (ते श्रुत्वा वच-नं तस्य ततस् तीर्थस्य मानद । कपाल-मोचनम् इति नाम चक्रुः समागताः) 9. 38. 4-20. E. Importance: Where Brah-man and the other gods, great ascetics (तपो-धनाः) and god Kārttikeya remain present for all the three divisions of time to do good to Bhārgava (त्रिसंध्यं किल भारत । सांनिध्यम् अकरोत् तत्र भार्गवप्रिय-काम्यया) 3. 81. 117; by bathing there one was freed of all sins 3. 81. 118. F. Epic relationship: Balarāma arrived at this तीर्थ and gave wealth according to the prescriptions to the high-souled Brāhmaṇas; after giving gifts and honouring the Brāhmaṇas, he pro-ceeded to the आश्रम of Ruṣaṅgu 9. 38. 4, 7, 21.
औजस: Aujasa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī 9. 45. 88; to the east of this तीर्थ was the Kurutīrtha (औजसस्य तु पूर्वेण कुरु-तीर्थम्) 3. 81. 144. B. Description: Excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 45. 93, 94; (तीर्थप्रवर) 9. 45. 89; holy (शृणु … पुण्यताम्) 9. 45. 88; shines by its own lustre (दीप्यते स्वेन तेजसा) 3. 81. 143; it was like another heaven (त्रिविष्टपम् इवापरम्) 9. 45. 89. C. Past events: (1) Formerly, at this तीर्थ Varuṇa, was anointed as the king of waters by the hosts of gods (औज-सं नाम तत् तीर्थं यत्र पूर्वम् अपां पतिः । अभिषिक्तः सुरगणैर् वरुणो भर-तर्षभ) 9. 45. 92; hence sacred to Varuṇa (औजसं वारुणं तीर्थम्) 3. 81. 143. (2) At this तीर्थ, Brahman and the other gods, and the sages anointed Guha (Kārtti-keya) as the general of the gods 3. 81. 143; 9. 45. 91; hence sacred also to Skanda 9. 45. 93; Kārttikeya gave here powers individually in the three worlds to the chiefs of the Nairṛtas (ऐश्वर्याणि च तत्रस्थो ददाव् ईशः पृथक् पृथक् । तदा नैरृतमुख्येभ्यस् त्रैलोक्ये पावकात्मजः) 9. 45. 90. D. Epic rela-tionship: Balarāma bathed there and wor-shipped Skanda; he gifted gold, garments and ornaments to Brāhmaṇas; he stayed there for a night, worshipped the excellent तीर्थ and bathed there (स्पृष्ट्वा तोयं च लाङ्गली); he became delighted and was happy 9. 45. 93-94.
औद्दालक: Auddālaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Resorted to by sages (मुनिनिषेवित); by taking a ceremonial bath there (तत्राभि-षेकम् कुर्वीत) one is freed of all sins 3. 82. 140.
औदुम्बर: Audumbara m. (pl.): Name of a Kṣatriya tribe. A. Location: Living probably in the north west; they are mentioned along with Bāhlikas and Kaśmīras (औदुम्बरा … बाह्लिकैः सह ॥ कश्मीराः … च) 2. 48. 12-13. B. Epic event: They brought tribute by hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 16.
औद्भिद: Audbhida1 m. (pl.): Name of a southern Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56. 5; (सौद्-भिदा नलकालकाः) 6. 10. 58.

Audbhida2 nt.: Name of a Varṣa in the Kuśadvīpa. A. Location: To the north of Jambu-dvīpa (उत्तरेषु तु … द्वीपेषु) 6. 13. 1; it is listed as the first among the collection of the seven Varṣas of Kuśadvīpa (औद्भिदं प्रथमं वर्षम् … सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्ज-काः) 6. 13. 12-13. B. People: In all the Varṣas of Kuśadvīpa, the gods, the Gandharvas and the people sport and enjoy together; no one meets with death; there are no Dasyus and no Mlecchas in those Varṣas; all people are fair and very delicate (एतेषु देवगन्धर्वाः प्रजाश् च जगती-श्वर । विहरन्ति रमन्ते च न तेषु म्रियते जनः ॥ न तेषु दस्यवः सन्ति म्लेच्छजात्यो ऽपि वा नृप । गौरप्रायो जनः सर्वः सुकुमारश् च पार्थिव ॥ ) 6. 13. 14-15.
औपक: Aupaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern peoples of the Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना भरतसत्तम) 6. 10. 63; (औपकाश् च कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 67.
औरसक: Aurasaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Among the exploits of Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛta-rāṣṭra mentions his victory over the Aurasakas (काश्मीरकान् औरसकान् … जित-वान् पुण्डरीकाक्षः) 7. 10. 16, 18.
और्णिक: Aurṇika m. (pl.): Name of a people. According to Mārkaṇḍeya, when the end of Kaliyuga will have arrived, such peoples as Aurṇikas and others, who are sinful and speakers of untruth will teach people the wrong way (अल्पावशिष्टे तु तदा युगान्ते भरतर्षभ) 3. 186. 24; (मिथ्या-नुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः ॥ … काम्बोजा और्णिकाः शूद्राः) 3. 186. 29-30.
